findings.title: Printed reconstruction matrix can be singular for Im omega > 0
findings.hypotheses: General Fourier reconstruction from (1.7), r>0, real smooth vortex profiles, n,alpha>0, Im omega>0; separate Assumption A not used in this general identity.
findings.evidence: q=1/2 Batchelor profiles, r=n=alpha=1, E=exp(-1), omega=-1/2+E+iE/2, ur=1, ur'=-1. Printed coefficient matrix rank 1, augmented rank 2; corrected determinant (-1+i)E nonzero and corrected velocity uz=utheta=(1-i)/2. A local analytic solution to the scalar ODE exists for these Cauchy data.
findings.impact: Printed recovery and its claimed nonvanishing fail; essential passage from radial solutions to Euler velocity modes must use the corrected formula.
findings.repair: Replace alpha^3 W r by -i alpha^2 W r and use determinant -(n^2/r+alpha^2 r)gamma. Independent exact pressure elimination confirms (1.9) and the Liouville transformation.
findings.limits: Not a global H01 eigenmode counterexample; not a counterexample to Theorem 1.1 or 1.2. Local algebraic reconstruction has no Assumption A restriction.

findings.title: The Sobolev semigroup bootstrap lacks a valid forcing estimate
findings.hypotheses: 1<Q<2, fixed Fourier mode; Lemma 3.5 requires LQ intersect Hk growth estimate.
findings.evidence: 1/p=1/2-1/Q is negative for every allowed Q (at Q=3/2 equals -1/6). The later forcing estimate targets L6/5 but is used for an L2 integral under a multiplication semigroup. Smooth divergence-free annulus family epsilon^(-5/6) chi((r-1)/epsilon)e^(2i theta)e_z has bounded L6/5 and L2 of order epsilon^(-1/3).
findings.impact: The written base step of the Hk semigroup bound is unsupported; this bound is used to construct high-order approximations for the main nonlinear theorem.
findings.repair: Use modewise velocity derivative gain: nonzero axial modes reduce to a 2D Bessel velocity kernel mapping LQ to L2; for zero axial modes combine L^(2Q/(2-Q)) velocity with decaying coefficients in L^(Q/(Q-1)). Rewrite the higher derivative bootstrap, and retain spectral slack 0<delta<2a-S.
findings.limits: No counterexample to the actual semigroup bound or nonlinear theorem. The annulus family disproves the unqualified embedding inference, not a claim that all such fields are the manuscript's specific forcing. Full replacement of the higher derivative proof not claimed.

findings.title: Real part of the potential has n-squared size within the claimed n-to-three-halves regime
findings.hypotheses: Any background satisfying the local Assumption A conditions; omega=omega_app; r_n=r0+c n^(-1/2), fixed 0<c<C^-1, n sufficiently large.
findings.evidence: With s=sqrt(b0)>0 and t=Lambda''(r0)c^2/2>0, Re k(r_n)/n^2 tends to p0*t^2*(t^2+3s^2)/(t^2+s^2)^2>0.
findings.impact: The displayed uniform O(n^(3/2)) upper size bound is false. Positive n^2 growth does not destroy the lower coercivity estimate.
findings.repair: Replace the two-sided size assertion by a bound Re k>=-C1 n^(3/2) on the negative part, combine with the positive imaginary part, and adjust the figure interpretation.
findings.limits: No counterexample to outer coercivity or ring-mode existence established.

findings.title: Wrong leading sign for the eigenvalue correction in the potential error
findings.hypotheses: r=r0, mu_m=O(n^-1/2), omega_hat=d n^-1/2 with fixed sufficiently small nonzero d in the allowed disk.
findings.evidence: Derivative at h=0 of 1+s^2/(-is-h)^2 equals -2i/s. True leading kerr=-2i p0 n^2 omega_hat/s; printed sign opposite. Difference of order n^(3/2) cannot enter the claimed O(n) remainder.
findings.impact: The displayed reduced identity requires a sign correction; absolute value estimates and nonzero leading coefficient remain.
findings.repair: Correct both f and g leading terms consistently; use integral complex Taylor remainder.
findings.limits: No change of qualitative Rouche zero count inferred from the sign alone.

findings.title: Complex Hermite argument requires a half-angle
findings.evidence: Printed G1(exp(i zeta)x)=exp(-i x^2/2) has modulus one and is not L2. Correct G1(exp(i zeta/2)x) has zero residual for the stated oscillator eigenvalue.
findings.impact: Printed eigenspace statement false; actual Weber ansatz and adjoint range formula elsewhere use the correct half-angle.

findings.title: Strict pitch variation excludes the advertised constant-pitch example
findings.hypotheses: Displayed Batchelor profiles with positive constant q.
findings.evidence: -(rV)'/W'=q for all r>0, so inf q=sup q; the middle strict inequality in Assumption A is not satisfied.
findings.impact: The example does not literally meet the printed theorem hypothesis.
findings.repair: Change middle strict inequality to <=; proof needs positive bounds rather than strict variation.
findings.limits: Not an admissible counterexample to the original theorem; exact scope mismatch and local correction.

focused_checks.reason: Primary read pp.3-6 and26-27, checked both momentum equations with exp(i(alpha*z-n*theta)), incompressibility and the exact retained script/output. Eliminating pressure gives upper-right -i*alpha*r*gamma, i.e. i*alpha*r*omega+i*n*alpha*V-i*alpha^2*r*W, not the printed alpha^3*r*W term. At q=1/2,r=n=alpha=1, the supplied upper-half-plane omega makes the printed columns opposite and the second equation forces uz=utheta, inconsistent with first right side -exp(-1). The corrected determinant (-1+i)exp(-1) and solution (1-i)/2 follow directly. Nonvanishing gamma and the nonzero leading radial coefficient give a local analytic ODE solution for the prescribed ur,ur'; these are appropriate to the general reconstruction before Assumption A, not a global eigenmode counterexample. The retained zero residuals for pressure elimination and Liouville substitution are valid counterevidence to a claimed failure of the radial equation itself. Major reflects the operative recovery step in Section3.2, with endpoint regularity still to be attached to the corrected formula.

Primary read the nonlinear assumptions on p.8 and the exact mode identity, Lemma3.5 and downstream integral on pp.30-33. For every 1<Q<2, the required 1/p=1/2-1/Q is negative. The p.31 L^(6/5) bound supplies no L2 bound under a pointwise matrix multiplier. The smooth fixed-mode annulus witness has measure proportional to epsilon, hence L^(6/5) size O(1) and L2 size epsilon^(-1/3); it is divergence-free because only its z component is nonzero and independent of z. Its limitation to the missing norm implication, not the actual forcing range, is correctly explicit. The proposed replacement uses nonzero-axial two-dimensional Bessel velocity kernels in L^s, 1/s=3/2-1/Q in (1/2,1), and for zero axial mode Q*=2Q/(2-Q), coefficient exponent Q/(Q-1)>2; boundedness at the axis and r^(-b-1) decay suffice for that coefficient norm. This supports the base estimate, not an unprovided full higher-derivative bootstrap. The positive slack must satisfy delta<2a-S and Picard time bounds are needed only for t<=0. Major is appropriate for an essential unsupported proof input without claiming the actual semigroup or nonlinear theorem is false.

Primary checked exact k,omega_app,p,b definitions on pp.3-6 and the full range and coercivity use on pp.16-17. For fixed 0<c<C^(-1), r_n=r0+c*n^(-1/2) eventually lies above C*n^(-3/4); omega=omega_app meets every B>=1 hypothesis. Taylor expansion gives gamma->t-i*s, with s=sqrt(b0)>0,t=Lambda''(r0)*c^2/2>0. Direct real-part evaluation gives p0*t^2*(t^2+3*s^2)/(t^2+s^2)^2>0 for Re k/n^2. Thus no fixed C rescues the asserted O(n^(3/2)) size. This positive term aids coercivity. On the small transition interval, bounded denominators and O(n^(-1/2)) perturbations give the stated lower negative-part bound, sufficient for the combination with Im k; no outer-coercivity counterexample is claimed. The report's separate far-field/order qualifications remain bounded limitations.

Primary read pp.5-6,10,20-21,36,38 and differentiated 1+s^2/(-i*s-h)^2: the derivative at zero is -2i/s. Subtracting the k0 containing mu_m leaves -2i*p0*n^2*omega_hat at leading order divided by s. A fixed sufficiently small nonzero d with omega_hat=d*n^(-1/2) obeys the frequency disk and yields an n^(3/2) discrepancy, beyond the O(n) remainder at r0. The negative sign already in A.4 is direct counterevidence against a mere sign-convention defense. Correcting both reduced coefficients f and g preserves the displayed absolute-value bounds and the nonzero linear leading term used in Rouche; it does not change the qualitative zero count by itself. An integral complex Taylor remainder is the justified formulation. Minor and the stated repair limits are appropriate.

Primary read Lemma2.5, its ODE proof, range formula and Corollary2.7 on pp.14-16. The allowed zeta=pi/4,m=1 gives the printed ground state exp(-i*x^2/2), of modulus one and outside L2. The half-angle state exp(-exp(i*pi/4)*x^2/2) is in L2 and direct differentiation gives eigenvalue -exp(i*pi/4) for d2/dx2-i*x2. The source's parabolic-cylinder change and range formula actually use the correct half-angle, limiting this to the inconsistent eigenspace/domain displays and repeated remark. No failure of the intended oscillator spectrum is inferred.

Primary checked the literal strict inf q<sup q on p.4 and the immediately advertised Batchelor profiles, then AppendixA.1 on p.38. Differentiating rV=q*(1-exp(-r^2)) and W=exp(-r^2) gives -(rV)'/W'=q for all r>0. Thus the middle strict inequality fails identically. The appendix only supplies the other local critical-point conditions and cannot repair that logical mismatch. Replacing this middle inequality by <= retains the positive upper/lower bounds used in the argument; this is an application/hypothesis correction, not an admissible counterexample to the originally stated theorem.
